Brazilian Grand Prix F1 2026 qualifying has been red flagged barely two minutes in for horrendous wet weather conditions. Rain was always a possibility and was forecast for Saturday at Interlagos, but torrential rain even as the session got underway caught out a host of cars and forced Formula 1 stewards into action. Eight cars: Kimi Antonelli's Mercedes, George Russell's Mercedes, Charles Leclerc's Ferrari, Isack Hadjar's Red Bull, the Alpines of Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto, Fernando Alonso's Aston Martin and the Cadillac of Valtteri Bottas all ventured out on intermediate tyres, but almost as soon as the cars hit the track it became clear that the conditions weren't driveable. Replays showed Lando Norris almost crashing, and Antonelli and Hadjar both laughed at how ridiculous the conditions were, also expressing the need for waterproofs.

Gabriel Bortoleto summed up the mood: "When I get out, I need to change my clothes, I'm completely wet!" Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton appeared to demonstrate their experience in F1 by not venturing out on track and remaining dry in the garage. There's no confirmed restart time yet as rain continues to pummel the track. Nico Hulkenberg was told the rain would fall this heavily for at least 10 minutes, with that radio message coming at 1808 UK time.

Esbjerg, Denmark, is using large electric heat pumps to extract heat from the North Sea and supply its district-heating network. During a two-hour winter test, seawater entered the system at 3.3°C and left at 1.2°C. The two heat pumps consumed 19.9 MW of electricity and supplied 55.2 MW of heat at a district-heating water temperature of 90°C. The difference, 35.3 MW, came from the seawater. The project team’s May 2025 operating report recorded a coefficient of performance, or COP, of 2.8. The figures describe that test, not annual average performance.

A heat pump transfers thermal energy from a colder source to a warmer destination. Its refrigerant absorbs heat at a temperature below that of the seawater, and an electrically driven compressor raises the temperature so the heat can enter the district network. Esbjerg uses carbon dioxide as its refrigerant in a high-pressure cycle. For each unit of electricity used by the compressors during the test, the plant delivered 2.8 units of heat. Resistance heating would have required 2.8 times as much electricity for the same heat output under those conditions.

For any savvy driver reluctant to cough up the eye-wateringly steep new-car asking prices today, a used car seems like a no-brainer option. However, buying a used car can be a minefield, too. Inspect the car too casually, and you could be flirting with unreliability. Luckily, the non-profit organization Consumer Reports (CR) helps buyers identify the vehicles that are much more likely to suffer unexpected faults or hidden issues — like burning oil in the case of gas-powered cars.

For those wondering, your car burning oil means oil is getting into the combustion chamber where it gets burned along with the air-fuel mixture. And since oil is essential for lubrication, cooling, and protecting the internal components inside the engine, your car burning or using too much oil can have serious consequences for its longevity. Naturally, this problem will cause oil levels to run low, reducing the lubrication inside the engine — also known as oil starvation . Without an effective lubrication film, the friction between moving parts inside the engine can accelerate wear on critical components, which can ultimately result in complete engine failure.

One of the most loved Japanese sports cars of the 21st century is the Nissan 350Z, partly because it was one of the badass villain cars in "The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift." But there's more to it than just that. While looks are subjective, it's hard to deny that it has aged rather nicely. It's also still genuinely affordable, making it one of the cheaper alternatives to Japanese performance cars that have skyrocketed in value .

But perhaps the main reason for its celebrated status is its engine: Nissan's VQ35. In essence, it's a 3.5-liter naturally aspirated V6 that produces around 287 horsepower in early 350Zs (or closer to 300 hp in the Nismo versions). Even by today's standards, the 350Z is quick: in Car and Driver 's testing, 0 to 60 miles per hour took 5.4 seconds, and it didn't top out until 156 mph. That's fast enough to red-face some of the greatest sport sedans of all time .

Like many automakers, Audi is listening to the backlash towards touch-sensitive controls. It’s been implementing subtle changes to its infotainment interface and other controls to improve the user interface, and we recently got a chance to try these updates in a 2027 Audi Q6 e-tron . The Q6 e-tron (and its A6 e-tron sedan stablemate) launched for the 2025 model year. After skipping the 2026 model year, the 2027 model-year examples of these EVs underwent changes to the steering wheel to incorporate more physical controls and to the MMI infotainment software to simplify the interface. Similar changes have been propagating across the Audi lineup since.

To start, there are new physical scroll wheels on the two steering-wheel spokes. The one on the left spoke controls the digital gauge cluster and cycles through different screens, while the one on the right spoke is a volume knob. There are still haptic buttons on the new wheel, but they’re responsive, and we prefer this setup to the previous one, which had only touch-sensitive buttons. The wheels are both simpler to use and have a satisfying click.

Sure, he was behind the creation of the most popular such vehicle, but the pony car concept was in the brewing stage years before the first-gen Mustang Mk1. That said, it's more nuanced than simply choosing one over the other, and it greatly depends on the application. First, the basics. Spark plugs in a gasoline engine play a key role because, without them, the gas-air mixture would not combust, and simply put, you'd go nowhere.

But even though they're a cornerstone of any gas engine — virtually as old as the invention itself — the tech behind them continues to develop. In the old days, spark plugs were made of copper. Copper is no longer used on modern cars because it wears out relatively quickly inside a cylinder of exploding gas that can routinely exceed 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit in normal operation. Plaintiff Jonathan Kamens has never been a customer at Cambridge Honda , and his cell phone number is on the National Do Not Call Registry, according to Automotive News . Henrik Fisker probably had no idea how fitting the name Karma would be when he launched the plug-in hybrid sedan in 2011 under his eponymous startup. Fisker’s venture wound up failing in 2014, but after Wanxiang Group, a Chinese automotive parts conglomerate, bought the assets, the car was reborn as the Karma Revero. The Revero has been built since 2016 and has undergone several updates, but the tiny California-based company has struggled to gain a foothold.

Now Karma Automotive is seeking to reinvent itself, and it will start by giving the plug-in hybrid sedan yet another reincarnation. Marques McCammon—previously of DaimlerChrysler, Roush, Saleen, and engineering firm Ricardo—joined as president of the company in 2023, and the 2027 Gyesera is the first product launched under his guidance. While it retains similarities to the sedans that preceded it, a lightly updated powertrain and a fresh design language aim to set the brand up for a brighter future. Driving a pre-production version of the Gyesera in and around Las Vegas, we discovered a car that feels special and provides enticing powertrain flexibility but that is still bound by some of the same flaws as its predecessors.
